STUDENT MANUAL Description The Student Manual serves as a comprehensive guide and resource for students at University of Cabuyao. It outlines the guidelines and expectations that govern student life and academic pursuits within the university. The manual covers a wide range of topics, including academic integrity, campus facilities, student rights and responsibilities, support services, and various important university regulations. It aims to empower students with the necessary information and resources to navigate their educational journey successfully, foster a positive learning environment, and promote personal and academic growth. MESSAGE FROM THE CITY MAYOR/ CHAIRMAN OF THE BOARD Sa ngalan ng lungsod at ng pinahahalagahang Board of Regents ng Unibersidad, kami ay taos-pusong bumabati at nagpapaabot ng mainit na pagtanggap sa inyo sa University of Cabuyao. Sa inyong paglalakbay sa larangan ng mas mataas na edukasyon, kami ay nagagalak na kayo ay maging mahalagang ambag sa aming aktibong akademikong komunidad. Maniwala kami na ang edukasyon ang pundasyon ng pag-unlad at susi sa pagbubukas ng inyong potensyal. Sa pamamagitan ng inyong dedikasyon, sipag, at uhaw sa kaalaman, magkakasama nating hinuhubog ang isang mas magandang kinabukasan para sa ating lungsod at sa mas malawak na pamayanan. Ang Student Manual, na hawak ninyo ngayon, ay isang mahalagang sanggunian na idinisenyo upang gabayan kayo sa inyong panahon ng pag-aaral, nagbibigay ng mahalagang impormasyon at mapagkukunan upang malampasan ang iba't ibang oportunidad at hamon na naghihintay sa inyo. Hinihikayat namin kayong gamitin nang lubusan ang inyong panahon sa UC (PnC). Isanib ninyo ang inyong sarili sa kayamanan ng mga karanasan sa pag-aaral, tanggapin ang iba't ibang perspektiba ng inyong mga kapwa mag-aaral, at makisangkot sa mga pinahahalagahang mga propesor na mag-aakay at magbibigay-inspirasyon sa inyo sa buong paglalakbay. Tandaan, ang edukasyon ay hindi limitado sa loob ng silid-aralan. Ito ay isang paglalakbay ng personal na pag-unlad, pagtuklas ng sarili, at pagbubuo ng makabuluhang ugnayan na magpapaanyo sa inyong pagkatao at magpapalawak ng inyong kaalaman. Nawa'y maging makulay ang inyong paglalakbay sa larangan ng pag-aaral, puno ng kasiyahan sa mga natuklasan, makabuluhang mga kaugnayan, at mga tagumpay na magpapabanaag ng kahalagahan ng inyong kinabukasan. HON. DENNIS FELIPE C. HAIN (Sgd) City Mayor/Chairman of the Board

MESSAGE FROM THE UNIVERSITY PRESIDENT It is with great pleasure and excitement that I welcome you to University of Cabuyao. As the President of this esteemed institution, I am honored to have you join our academic community, where knowledge, growth, and excellence are celebrated. As you embark on your academic journey, I encourage you to embrace the spirit of curiosity, critical thinking, and lifelong learning. Our distinguished faculty members are dedicated to nurturing your intellectual curiosity, challenging your perspectives, and inspiring you to reach new heights of academic achievement. Seize every opportunity to engage in research, collaborate with peers, and participate in experiential learning activities that will broaden your horizons and shape your future career path. text: OUR HISTORY

section_path: OUR HISTORY
text: On April 16, 2003, then-municipal mayor Proceso D. Aguillo signed Municipal Ordinance No. 2003-059, "Ordinance Establishing the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao (University of Cabuyao) and Other Purposes," creating the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao (PnC). The institution began offering classes in business administration, information technology, education, nursing, and midwifery in June 2003. Before the Pamantasan ng Cabuyao was founded, the Laguna State Polytechnic University (LSPU) had a satellite campus at the Cabuyao National High School. A memorandum of understanding between the mayor of Cabuyao Municipality and the LSPU president served as the basis for the LSPU's operations. The LSPC-Cabuyao Campus began its operation in 1993 and ended on March 31, 2003. In the latter half of 2002, faculty and students at LSPC protested against the LSPC president's leadership. With the support of the majority of students, who were mostly Cabuyeños, the protest was found by the Sangguniang Bayan of Cabuyao to be true and based on facts. It caused the memorandum of agreement to be terminated, and the only option left to the mayor's administration was to establish Cabuyao Community College.

section_path: OUR HISTORY
text: In light of the anticipated closure of LSPC-Cabuyao, faculty members under the leadership of Charlemagne Lavina and Frank Parao aided the mayor's office and advised them that the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila (PLM) is the model school for local colleges. Dr. Benjamin Tayabas, who was president of PLM at the time, helped the town of Cabuyao and personally oversaw the establishment of the institution. He recommended calling it Pamantasan ng Cabuyao. Municipal Ordinance No. 2003-059 was enacted by the Sanguniang Bayan on April 15, 2003. The following day, Mayor Proceso D. Aguillo gave his approval to the same. Pamantasan ng Cabuyao was personally inaugurated by no less than President Gloria Macapagal Arroyo on June 19, 2003 on the occasion of the 107th birthday of Dr. Jose Rizal and officially started its operations on July 31, 2003, the birthday of its founding mayor. In 2017, the university received its Commission on Higher Education (CHED) Institutional Recognition, becoming one of the few local colleges and universities (LCUs) to receive such recognition. The university was awarded by the Duterte Administration the right to avail of the FREE COLLEGE EDUCATION or the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary

section_path: OUR HISTORY
text: Education (UNIFAST) under the Republic Act 10931 – becoming one of the 76 LCUs in the country to be given such right to free education in 2019. To date, PnC has been awarded by ALCUCOA with twelve (12) Level 2 and two (2) Level 1 programs. The higher level of accreditation is a testament to the university's commitment to providing free quality education, especially to its talented marginalized student populace. Today, PnC is one of the few leading local colleges and universities in the Philippines with level 2 accredited programs. The university produced topnotchers in the fields of education, nursing, and engineering. Forward-looking, PnC envisions itself becoming the premier leading local university in Region IV by further elevating its academic standards, thereby producing value-laden and globally competent graduates and continuously striving for improvement in quality services in instruction, research, and extension. PnC commits itself to the holistic education of every "Dangal ng Bayan", thereby producing graduates that bring pride and honor to the nation.

section_path: UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
text: THE UNIVERSITY LOGO The logo features a green circular outer layer. It symbolizes the university's commitment to environmental sustainability and community development by representing the Cabuyao land. The six-pointed stars within the layer represent the University's founders, implying that the University was founded by a group of six people who shared a common vision and goal for the school. The inner layer of the logo depicts Cabuyao's legendary Kampanang Ginto. A shield-shaped design with a white-gray background is contained within the bell. The shield is blue to represent the sky, which represents the pursuit of knowledge and wisdom. This also emphasizes the University's commitment to produce graduates that bring pride and honor to the nation. Within the shield is the year 2003, the year of the University's establishment. The image of the Cabuyao Municipal Hall below represents the university's close relationship with the local government and commitment to serving the community. On top of the Cabuyao City Hall is an engineering triangle that represents

section_path: UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
text: strength, stability, and balance. It also symbolizes the university's dedication to providing a solid foundation for engineering education. The caduceus is a well-known ancient symbol associated with medicine and healthcare. It also symbolizes the university's strong focus on health-related programs. The stylized flame in the middle of the shield represents the spirit of innovation and creativity. The flame also represents the university's commitment to promoting entrepreneurship and inspiring its students to be leaders in their respective fields. Under it is an open book, which represents the pursuit of knowledge and the importance of education in the university's mission. The atoms are written in an open book and convey the university's emphasis on science, research, and the pursuit of knowledge. The gear on top represents the university's commitment to providing education in engineering, technology, and innovation. The gavel represents authority, order, and leadership and its intention to offer preparatory programs for law academic program. The lighting represents the university's dedication to fostering creativity, inspiration, and new ideas. The quill pen is associated with the University's arts and sciences program. A dove holding an olive branch represents the element of peace. These symbols represent the university's dedication to fostering peaceful coexistence and understanding among various cultures and communities. Below the image is the university's mantra, "Peace, Prosperity, and Service," which conveys the university's commitment to fostering economic growth and development on a local and global scale, as well as the university's ethos of giving back to society and making a positive difference in the lives of others.

section_path: UNIVERSITY SYMBOLS
text: UNIVERSITY MACE The University of Cabuyao mace is a regally designed symbol of academic authority and prestige that embodies the rich heritage and traditions of the university. With its prominent university emblem displayed atop a polished wood staff adorned with intricate carvings, the mace serves as a visual reminder of the institution's commitment to providing quality education, fostering intellectual growth, and shaping the future of its students. Displayed during ceremonial occasions, the mace inspires a sense of pride and unity among the university community, reinforcing the collective commitment to academic excellence and the pursuit of knowledge. UNIVERSITY MEDALLION The University of Cabuyao medallion worn by the University President is a symbol of esteemed leadership and authority. The medallion showcases the university's emblem or crest at the forefront. Crafted from high-quality materials, the medallion exudes a sense of prestige and significance. As a distinguished accessory worn by the University President, it represents the highest level of academic and administrative responsibility. It is a visual embodiment of the university's values, traditions, and commitment to excellence, symbolizing the leader's role in guiding and shaping the institution's future.

section_path: INSTITUTIONAL PHILOSOPHY & OBJECTIVES
text: INSTITUTIONAL VISION A premier educational institution of higher learning in Region IV, developing globally-competitive and value-laden professionals and leaders instrumental to community development and nation building. INSTITUTIONAL MISSION As an institution of higher learning, PnC is committed to equip individuals with knowledge, skills and values that will enable them to achieve their professional goals and provide leadership and service for national development. INSTITUTIONAL QUALITY POLICY Pamantasan ng Cabuyao commits to adhering to statutory and regulatory requirements, promoting high levels of customer engagement, and maintaining an effective quality management system through periodic review and communication of quality objectives for continuous improvement of quality services in instruction, research, and extension. INSTITUTIONAL QUALITY OBJECTIVES 1. To promote analytical thinking among the faculty and students for continuing intellectual growth and advancement of learning and research. 2. To develop the youth to become responsible leaders, as well as productive and actively involve citizens of the local and global community with good values and excellent character. 3. To preserve, enrich, and transmit the historical, cultural heritage, and desirable Filipino values and character. 4. To nurture an integrated multi-disciplinary university that promotes excellence in instruction, research, and extension. 5. To be the research and development arm of the local government unit. 6. To strengthen industry-academe-LGU linkage in order to realize the vision and mission of the University INSTITUTIONAL CORE VALUES As a God-fearing institution respecting multi-faith of people, PnC adheres to the following core values: Personal Dignity, Nurturing Community, and Commitment to Excellence

section_path: PART 1. ADMISSION & ENROLLMENT
text: The University of Cabuyao has established clear and transparent admission and enrollment guidelines to ensure a fair and efficient process for prospective students. To be admitted into the university, applicants must meet the specified academic requirements, which may vary depending on the desired program of study. T Once admitted, students proceed with the enrollment process, where they officially register for their chosen courses and programs. It is essential for students to carefully follow the provided guidelines and deadlines to secure their place and successfully enroll in the University of Cabuyao. By implementing these admission and enrollment guidelines, the University of Cabuyao aims to maintain a systematic and organized process that ensures a seamless transition for students from application to enrollment, ultimately allowing them to embark on their academic journey at the university.

text: CHAPTER II STUDENT ENROLMENT PNC:AA-GU-19 Section 1. General Policies 1. section_path: PART 2. ACADEMIC GUIDELINES
text: The University of Cabuyao has established clear and comprehensive academic policies to ensure the smooth and fair administration of student-related matters. These policies cover various areas, including student examinations, issuance of academic records, transfer of credits in collegiate programs, semestral academic honors, grading systems for senior high school, college, and graduate school, management of educational trips and off-campus activities for both college and senior high school students, as well as senior high school and college graduation requirements. These guidelines are designed to uphold academic integrity, maintain consistent standards, and support the overall educational experience and success of students at the University of Cabuyao.

text: CHAPTER I STUDENT EXAMINATION PNC:AA-GU-11 Section 1. General Policies 1. Uploading and administration of tests are facilitated thru the iMPnC (PinnaCle). Teaching personnel may opt to administer the examination onsite or thru other external learning tool such as Google Form and MS Form, among others. 2. Examinations must be reviewed by the Department Chair two weeks before the scheduled examination before uploading to Pinnacle or administering in other forms. 3. The weight of examination in the grading system is as follows: a. College (For lecture, it is 50% of the grading system and for laboratory it is 60% of the grading system). b. Graduate School (It is 40% of the grading system) c. Senior High School (Quarterly assessment is 25% for core subjects, 30% for academic track, and 20% for Technical-Vocational and Livelihood. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Senior High School a. Quarterly examinations are given in all subjects. b. Examinations are validated by the Principal or SHS Coordinator. c. Type of Examinations. The type of examinations is usually situational analysis and application which bring out critical thinking and related skills among the learners. d. Post-Test Evaluation. Learners are allowed to countercheck the answers in the examination thru the LMS or other platforms adapted by the Senior High School.

text: e. Grading System. It adopts a based zero grading system. 2. College a. The examination schedules are announced by the Office of the University Registrar and the Dean's Office before the start of classes. b. Examinations in college are scheduled by the Registrar and Academic Head for six days based on the actual class schedule so as not to have conflicts. c. The Deans shall observe departmental examination. d. Other evaluative measures such as cultural presentation, immersion, recitation, or quizzes shall be reflected in the e-class record (igrade.pnc.edu.ph) with corresponding weight or percentage to complete the final grade. Quizzes must be explicitly written on the class record and shall always be part of the grade. Project not included in the Outcomes-Based Teaching and Learning Plan (OBTLP) is not allowed. e. This must be part of the OBTLP. f. Written complaints on test checking can be entertained before the final recording on the class record. g. Missed Examinations. A student who misses a major examination automatically obtains a raw score of zero unless his/her failure to take the test is excused. h. Special Examinations. Special examination may be given to a student who missed a major examination upon presentation of the approved application form (PNC:AA-FO-32). i. The examination must be taken not later than seven

Students who have qualified in academic and non-academic competitions may be requested by the Department Chair/Coordinator to take the examination until the encoding of grades. i. Missed Quizzes. In order to prepare for the board/licensure examinations, graduating students in BS Accountancy, Nursing, Psychology, Education, and Engineering are expected to take mock board exams. Results of the mock board exams are provided to the students within a week or according to a set schedule, and students who do not pass are offered intervention programs by the respective department. During their consultation schedule, teaching personnel should discuss the corrected examination with students so that they are aware of their areas for improvement in the relevant course.

text: CHAPTER III RETENTION GUIDELINE FOR ALL ACADEMIC PROGRAMS PNC:AA-GU-10 Section 1. General Policies 1. The program requires that students must adhere to the retention guideline upon admission. 2. The retention guideline of the University applies to the first, second, and third-year students of the different colleges and Senior High School, providing a suitable and effective provision. 3. The guideline aims to provide suitable and effective interventions to encourage students to meet the requirements of their respective fields. Its purpose is to filter out students who are not meeting the minimum course requirements, and for board programs, to increase the likelihood of graduates passing board exams. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Classification of Students for Board and Non-Board Programs a. With Good Standing. Any student who receives passing grades or higher in all courses enrolled for the semester shall be classified as good standing. b. Warning. A student who did not pass 25% of his/her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be warned by the Dean and Department Chair using the prescribed form (PNC:AA-FO-18) to improve his/her work. The student shall be asked to write the promissory letter expressing intent to improve his/ her grade/s or risk being put on probation. The letter shall

A student who did not pass more than 50% of his/ her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be put on probation. A consultation with the student and parent shall be facilitated by the Program Chair and Dean. An Academic Contract (PNC:AA-FO-19) shall be signed by all parties concerned. His/her load shall be reduced by three units. A probationary students who receives a warning on the following semester will be dismissed from the university. Students who receive an Inc grade will be assigned a Probationary status unless they complete their studies before the enrollment period. Academic Competency Examination for Students (ACES) shall be given to those who have completed their first and second year curriculum. Student who will fail the said examination shall be given Probationary Status. A consultation with the student and parent shall be facilitated by the Department Chair and Dean. An Academic Contract (PNC:AA-FO-19) shall be signed by all parties concerned. d. Dismissal. A student who did not pass 75% of his/her courses enrolled in one given semester shall be dismissed immediately. Students shall be permanently barred from readmission to any programs of the University. Parents/Guardian shall be informed of the status of the concerned student. 2. The rule on dismissal does not apply to the following: a. Students whose grades of 5.0 were incurred due to incorrect encoding of the teacher; and b. text: CHAPTER VI MANAGEMENT OF EDUCATIONAL TRIPS, AND OTHER OFF-CAMPUS ACTIVITIES OF COLLEGE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS PNC:AA-GU-14 Section 1. General Policies 1. Educational tour refer to curricular off-campus learning activities involving mobility of students with the supervision of authorized personnel outside the premises of the institution which lasts for more than one (1) day, and involves relatively more places of destination than a field trip in accordance with specific degree program requirements (CMO 63 s. 2017). This covers visits to reputable firms or government sites; culture and arts-related activities such as visits to museums, cultural sites, landmarks, and other related venues; and plant industry visit, host training establishment visits, and other related visits. 2. Field trip refer to curricular off-campus learning activities involving mobility of students with the supervision of authorized personnel outside the premises of the institution but is of relatively shorter duration usually lasting for only one (1) day, and with fewer places of destination (CMO 63 s.2017). 3. According to CHED Memorandum Order No. 63, s. 2017, as well as CHED Memorandum Order 26, s. 2015, and subsequent memoranda in 2018, the University is required to abide by the policies and guidelines for local off-campus activities and international trips for undergraduate and graduate students. 4. The University is responsible for designing, determining, and approving off-campus activities that align with the curriculum requirements and the University's philosophy and objectives. The design of these activities should also consider their relevance to the program.

text: 5. Prior to joining any educational tours or off-campus activities, all college and graduate students must provide a medical clearance to ensure their fitness for participation. 6. The Entrepreneurial and Business Development Department, through an Accredited Service Provider, must coordinate in advance and properly with local government units, including obtaining a letter of acknowledgement from the concerned government agency before any scheduled educational tours, field trips, or related off-campus activities. 7. However, they cannot be used as a substitute for major exams to compel students to participate in non-compulsory educational activities. 10. Whenever possible, the proposed activities should be scheduled in a way that minimizes any negative impact on other academic activities. 11. Consent from parents, guardians, or spouses (if applicable) must be obtained before conducting any curricular or non-curricular off-campus activities. 12. For security reasons, only officially enrolled students in the course are allowed to participate in curricular and non-curricular off-campus activities. 13. A general orientation must be conducted for concerned students, faculty, and stakeholders before conducting any educational tours, field trips, or other related off-campus activities.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS
text: Welcome to the Student Success section of the Student Manual. At Pamantasan ng Cabuyao, we are committed to providing you with an enriching educational experience that extends beyond the classroom. We believe that your success as a student is not solely measured by grades, but by your holistic growth, personal development, and achievement of your goals. This section of the manual aims to equip you with valuable insights, strategies, and resources that will empower you to thrive academically, socially, and personally during your time at PnC. We understand that each student's journey is unique, and we are here to support you every step of the way. Student success is about more than just completing coursework and earning a degree. It encompasses your ability to navigate the challenges and opportunities that arise, build meaningful connections with peers and mentors, and cultivate essential skills that will serve you well in your future endeavors. Remember, your success as a student is a partnership between you and the institution. It requires dedication, resilience, and a proactive approach to your education. By taking advantage of the opportunities available to you and embracing a growth mindset, you will not only excel academically but also develop into a well-rounded individual prepared for the challenges and triumphs that lie ahead. We are excited to embark on this journey with you and celebrate your achievements along the way. Together, let us create a vibrant and supportive community where student success is not just a goal, but a reality for each and every one of you.

This period is divided into general and special preparatory stage. There are two and a half to three months in the general preparatory stage, which is always longer than the second stage. It guarantees quantitative work; when the player's capacity for training load changes, a higher amount of training is always feasible. The major goal of this exercise is to maintain the players' physical condition at all times. The main emphasis of the training is on the outcomes of games and other activities. d. section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS > Section 1. General Policies
text: CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS PNC:SDAS-GU-08 Section 1. General Policies 1. The establishment and operation of student organizations in all colleges and universities are governed by the then Department of Education, Culture and Sports Department Order No. 61 s. 1985 which provides rules and regulations concerning student organizations and their activities within the school campus. 2. Students who want to form a student organization should follow the regulations promulgated by the University through the Student Affairs and Services Department (SASD). 3. The University reserves the right not to admit organizations espousing goals/activities contrary to the philosophy and objectives of the institution. 4. All recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils are directly under the jurisdiction and supervision of the SASD. 5. All guidelines governing the recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall be made by the SASD. 6. Membership fees may be collected among students as indicated in the Constitution and By-Laws and as needed. This shall be coordinated with the SASD Director. Management of fund shall be monitored by the Adviser and the SASD Director.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Application for Recognition a. Recognition of student organizations is made official once they are given the certificate of recognition. Official recognition shall be effective for one academic year or one semester only under special circumstances. b. The following organizations should seek approval for recognition from SASD: i. newly-formed organizations; ii. organizations which became inactive for at least one semester; and iii. probationary organizations, which include suspended organizations that have been existing for two years. c. Any group of at least 20 members intending to form a student organization may apply to SASD. d. The following documents must be prepared at the time of application: i. Accomplished application form to be issued by the SASD (PNC:SDAS-FO-15); ii. Proposed Constitution and by-laws; iii. Student Leader's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-16); iv. Adviser's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-17); v. List of Active Members (PNC:SDAS-FO-18); vi. Adviser's Agreement Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-19) vii. Annual Project Plan (PNC:SDAS-FO-20) e. The SASD shall deliberate on the merit of the applicant organization based on the documents submitted. The applicant organization shall be informed of the results of the deliberation (approved or disapproved) five days after the submission of the requirements. PNC:SDAS-FO-15 Page 2 shall be used by the SASD Director in evaluating the applicant student organization.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: f. The recommended list of recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall be endorsed to Vice President for Student Affairs and Auxiliary Services for approval. Once approved, the Certificate of Recognition shall be given during the recognition ceremony. 2. Renewal of Recognition a. Recognized student organizations and student councils applying for renewal of recognition should submit the following to SASD: i. Renewal Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-15); ii. Student Leader's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-16); iii. Adviser's Profile with 1 x 1 recent photo (PNC:SDAS-FO-17); iv. List of Active Members (PNC:SDAS-FO-18); v. Activity Financial Statement (PNC:SDAS-FO-21). b. The renewal of recognition/accreditation of student organization is a precondition for its operation in the University. A Certificate of Recognition shall be given to the organization's full compliance with the requirements. c. Non-compliance with the requirements and procedures of the evaluation process also means automatic disqualification of the student organizations concerned. d. Student organizations who failed to meet the criteria for evaluation set by the SASD shall be dropped from the roster. They are allowed to re-apply for recognition after a year of reprieve observing the procedures for Application for Recognition. e. When the organization, which has ceased its activities for at least one year desires to operate again, the guidelines on Application shall be followed.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER III RECOGNITION AND RENEWAL OF STUDENT ORGANIZATIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: 3. Recognition Status. Student organizations which qualify for recognition may do the following: a. text: 6. Selection of RSO, CSG, SC, and USG Adviser a. The recognized student organizations, college student government, and student councils shall select their adviser according to the qualifications set forth by SASD. b. Any full-time non-teaching and teaching personnel may perform advising role to the student organizations as long as he/she meets the qualifications set forth by SASD. c. Each student organization selects an adviser subject to the approval of the SASD Director. d. Student organizations must have only one adviser. An adviser should only have one student organization to be monitored every academic year. e. The following are the qualification standards for advisers: i. S/he is a full-time teaching or non-teaching personnel in the University. ii. For academic-related organizations, an adviser must have an academic preparation, professional training, or experience related to the organization s/he is advising. iii. For non-academic student organizations, the adviser must be knowledgeable of the organization's area of specialization. iv. S/he has at least a "Very Good" evaluation rating based on previous advisees' evaluation (PNC:SDAS-FO-22) v. S/he has a good moral character, with personal integrity and has not been subjected to any grievance or disciplinary proceedings during the period of his /her employment in the University. vi. S/he has strong commitment and willingness to devote time and effort to student development. vii. S/he has good leadership and interpersonal skills and is committed in maintaining harmonious and pleasant personal and official relations with other teaching and non-teaching personnel and administrators of the University.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER IV SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: CHAPTER IV SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-09 Section 1. General Policies 1. In collaboration with the Student Scholarship and Financial Assistance Officer, the Director of Student Affairs and Services will process student applications for government-sponsored scholarships in accordance with their guidelines. 2. All students are eligible to apply for any scholarship as long as they meet the program's eligibility requirements. 3. No scholar is permitted to accept more than one scholarship from the university. A student is eligible to receive or apply for additional scholarships offered by various private and public organizations. 4. If the grantee does not adhere to the terms of the scholarship grant and/or in the event of a breach of the University's current policies stated below, the scholarship may be terminated. This will result in forfeiture of the scholarship once the VP SDAS's decision has been authorized. 5. Following disqualification, a student is not eligible to rejoin the same scholarship program. However, if spots are still available for the scholarship being applied on, resigned scholars may still submit an application. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) for Filipino citizens a. University Registrar shall facilitate the implementation of RA 10931 Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act of 2017. b. For repeat courses, the student shall pay the corresponding rate per course.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 1. General Policies
text: CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES PNC:SDAS-GU-10 Section 1. General Policies 1. Student activities can be conducted and/or participated in by securing the approval of the authorities concerned through SASD. 2. All proposed projects and activities shall be reflected in the Annual Project Plan (PNC:SDAS-FO-20). Once approved, the organization shall submit individual Letter of Request (LR) (PNC:AF-FO-30) for each activity. 3. In cases of activities which are not reflected in the project plan form, Letter of Request (LR) (PNC:AF-FO-30) shall be submitted to the same office at least 45 working days before the conduct of the proposed activity. A letter of justification shall be submitted if the organization failed to comply with the given period of time. 4. Submission of other pertinent requirements and observance of all SASD prescribed rules and regulations in the conduct of such functions/assemblies are vital for the approval of the proposed activity. 5. Activities held without approval are considered illegal and may be considered a ground for administrative sanction of the proposed activity. 6. In case the student functions/assemblies shall require the use of campus facilities online or remotely, a separate arrangement with the authorities concerned shall be made by the sponsoring organization or group as soon as the SASD has approved the activity.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 1. General Policies
text: 7. No student activities shall be conducted one week before the start of any major examination. 8. Student organization shall not use the name "Pamantasan ng Cabuyao," its official logo, in any activity (i.e., fair, seminar, fieldtrip, tour, contract, announcement, etc.) or on any manufactured item unless duly authorized by the SASD. 9. All activities shall secure evaluation from its participants using the official form of the University.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Social Affairs a. A social affair/concert shall be supervised by the adviser and concerned authorities. The services of police officers/barangay officials, in addition to security guards, may be employed for the activity. b. These events shall not go beyond 11pm and it must be ensured that security measures are strictly observed and directly supervised by the adviser and the officers of the concerned student organization. In exigency cases, activities that will extend the allowable hour shall be approved by the VP SDAS. 2. Fund-Raising Projects/Solicitation a. A fund-raising activity must be motivated by an objective consistent with the philosophy and objectives of the University and the thrust of the sponsoring recognized student organization. b. Duly recognized student organizations may be allowed to sponsor only one major fundraising activity per semester. These shall be monitored by the SASD Director and Adviser. c. Tickets or any related materials shall not be released without prior approval from SASD. d. Application for fund-raising activities shall include activity objectives, ticket prizes (if applicable), beneficiary, manner as to how the funds shall be used, financial projection, and budget plan, and brief description of how the project shall be implemented. e. In case of a raffle project, prizes must be displayed at some strategic place on campus before the raffle takes place. If the prize is in the form of cash or small items, such should be publicly announced through posters before the raffle date. The list of winners must likewise be publicly proclaimed through notices on the bulletin boards around the campus. f. An Activity Financial Statement (PNC:SDAS-FO-21) duly certified by the Adviser and the Dean (for academic organizations) of the fundraising activity shall be submitted to

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: the SASD within ten (10) working days after the activity. Failure to do so shall be a ground for withdrawal of the recognition of the organization. g. All monetary solicitations should be duly reviewed by SASD and VPSDAS, endorsed by the Executive Vice President and approved by the University President. 3. Symposia, Fora, and Other Seminar Workshop-Type Activities. a. Symposium, forum, etc. drawn from a desire to fulfill the University philosophy and objectives may be implemented by the concerned student organization. b. Activities of this nature, which are intellectually stimulating, must be well- planned, properly motivated by a genuine need to supplement regular curricular programs, and sponsored by an organization directly connected with the institution. c. Persons to be invited as speakers shall be those who have distinguished themselves in their respective discipline or endeavor and shall contribute to the educational objectives of the University as well as the sponsoring organization. d. Institution may withhold its approval when it has been established that the invited speaker is: i. a person who advocates or espouses the use of violence and disruptive measures to achieve his/her end; and/or ii. a person who has maliciously damaged the good name of the institution and its administration. 4. Outreach Activities a. Outreach activities are charitable acts performed by student organizations with communities outside PnC-UC as the main beneficiaries. Application for approval shall follow the same procedures as other activities. However, outreach activities should also be coordinated with and endorsed by the Community Extension and Services (CES) Department prior to the SASD final approval.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER V MANAGING IN-PERSON AND REMOTE STUDENT ACTIVITIES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: 5. Participation in Outside Activities a. PnC (UC) students may participate in any outside activity-contest, play, band, exhibition games, symposium, society or group as representatives of the University, provided, that they have a written authorization from the SASD and VP SDAS and the Academic Head concerned. b. text: CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS PNC:SDAS-GU-11 Section 1. General Policies 1. SASD through the SCOMELEC facilitates the Student Elections from the call for candidacy to the proclamation of winners guided by the principle that the University is a venue for the leadership development of the youth and that they have the right for organization and self-government. 2. Composition, Qualifications, and Duties and Responsibilities of SCOMELEC a. The SCOMELEC shall be composed of the Chairman and the Commissioners. b. The SCOMELEC shall be composed of enrolled college and SHS students who are willing to take part in facilitating the student election except for the following: i. Those who run for the specific position; ii. Those who are incumbent officer for current year of election; and iii. Those who have derogatory and disciplinary record. c. Following are the duties and responsibilities of the SCOMELEC. i. Oversee the planning, implementation, and evaluation of student election activities ii. Ensure proper channeling and coordination of information and activities of the group iii. Organizes student leadership colloquium or campaign forum and meeting de avance iv. Ensures equal opportunities for all candidates during the event v. Orients candidates of the Election Code, decorum, and

Election dates shall be determined by the SCOMELEC. 5. Candidates shall be given five working days to campaign before the first day of election. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Registration of Political Party a. Any group of bona fide students of PNC (UC) may form a political party. b. All political parties, however, are subject to screening of the SCOMELEC. The following are the requirements necessary for the screening of the parties seeking for recognition: i. Conformity to the prescribed guidelines of the SCOMELEC ii. List of candidates and campaign manager iii. Compiled requirements of all student election candidates iv. Platform/Plan of Action c. All requirements shall be submitted on the date set by the SCOMELEC. d. Core Positions for College Student Government and University Student Government to be filled out are as follows: i. President ii. Vice President iii. Secretary iv. Treasurer v. Auditor

SCOMELEC shall deliberate whether the aspiring candidate/s shall be allowed to pursue candidacy or be denied of it depending on its recommendation.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies

The candidate shall attend the Candidate's Orientation to be conducted by the SCOMELEC where they will be informed of the schedule of student-election related activities, campaign guidelines, and proper decorum as a candidate. g. The candidate shall participate in the scheduled campaign forum or meeting de avance. Campaign materials may also be uploaded in social media and online platforms upon approval of the SASD Director. 3. Candidacy Requirements a. Applicant candidates who are incumbent officers of any student organization and student council may continue with the regular functions provided that their activities will not promote their candidacy. b. Documentary Requirements.Applicant candidates shall submit the following requirements: i. Duly signed Certificate of Candidacy (COC) with Parent's signature ii. Certified True Copy of Grades or compcards during the last two semesters of attendance iii. Certificate of Good Moral Character iv. Recent 2x2 colored picture attached to the COC v. Students who have record of any serious or major infraction inside or outside the University shall not be allowed to run for any elective position

text: c. Academic Requirements i. All students who are interested to run and be elected for certain position in the organization must be in good academic standing i.e. have no failing grades in the last two semesters. ii. The grades in Physical Education (PE) and National Service Training Program (NSTP) shall be considered in the computation of the weighted average. The student should not have incurred a failure or dropped in any subject including PE and NSTP during the previous two semesters of their attendance. iii. Probationary students are not allowed to run for any elective position. Students who have record of any infraction inside or outside the school will not also be allowed to run for any elective position. iv. Transferees should have at least two semesters of residency in the University before they will be allowed to run. v. All the election processes of the academic and non-academic organizations shall be facilitated by the SCOMELEC. vi. Candidates for elective position shall follow the rules and regulations set by the SCOMELEC on the process of elections. vii. Once elected or appointed as an officer, the student must maintain a passing grade in all courses. S/he must be of good moral character. viii. Student leaders shall submit every semester to their adviser of the organization a photocopy of their compcard. The SASD Director monitors the academic standing of the officers and recommends action to the VPSDAS. ix. If the officer incurs a failing grade in any of the enrolled courses, s/he will be placed on probation. If placed on probation, s/he will be given another semester to improve his/her grades. If academic progress is not made after the prelim period of the succeeding semester, the individual will be required to resign from his/her position immediately. x. In cases where there will be vacancy because of the previously mentioned reason, the organization's rule on

text: filling out of vacancy will be observed as mentioned in their respective constitution and by-laws. d. Campaign Guidelines i. All candidates are enjoined to engaged in wholesome and peaceful campaigning emphasis on merits as candidates and on what service the person or party may contribute for the welfare and betterment of all sectors of the institution. ii. The campaign period shall take place three weeks before the actual election. iii. Candidates and/or parties are prohibited from engaging in dirty or malicious campaign in any means that will impinge the honor and dignity of their fellow candidates or parties or the name of PNC (UC). Acts that are inimical to a wholesome campaign are as follows: name calling, libelous accusations, false and grossly exaggerated claims devoid of material proofs, personal attacks on the private life/family of any candidate, destruction of campaign paraphernalia of other candidates or parties and vandalism in any form (social media, print, verbal, physical, etc). iv. Participation in the campaign and election process is strictly limited in the students of PNC (UC). Non-students, including alumni, are prohibited from meddling in the electoral process. Parties and candidates are also prohibited from involving non-PNC (UC) students in the said activities. v. Parties/individuals are prohibited from conducting boisterous and noisy forms of campaign in in-person or virtual University activities and spaces. vi. Vote buying or any form of monetary inducement of voters is strictly prohibited. Violation of this provision shall mean absolute disqualification. vii. Coercion, harassment, intimidation of voters or candidates of another party is strictly prohibited. viii. Candidates and/or parties shall be prohibited from enjoining teaching and non-teaching personnel on stating comments which may influence the voter's decision. ix. Any violation in the prescribed campaign conduct shall be subjected to immediate disqualification if proven after due process of SCOMELEC

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: e. Public Debate / Campaign Forum i. A public debate may be organized by SCOMELEC for the contending parties and independent candidates aside from the traditional Meeting de Avance. ii. The SCOMELEC shall act as moderator of the debate. f. Canvassing of Votes i. The canvassing of votes is automatic and the results are computer generated. ii. For the canvassing process to be acknowledged as fair and honest, the parties are allowed to assign a maximum of two representatives to verify the election results. iii. Candidates for each particular position who have received the most number of votes will be proclaimed the winner even if there is only one party running for election. However, the candidate must receive 50% plus one vote of the total student population of the institution who voted for University Student Government and 50% plus one votes of the total student population who voted of their respective college/SHS. iv. When two or more candidates have received an equal number of votes which would entitle them to a position, the winner shall be chosen in such a manner that they may agree upon like draw lots or toss coin. Should they reach an agreement, the SCOMELEC reserves the right to decide who the winner is after due process. g. Proclamation i. The proclamation of winners shall be made within the day of election upon the authenticated official printed result as acknowledged and signed by the SCOMELEC Officials, Party/Candidate Representative, SASD Director, and Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services. ii. The newly-elected officers shall be inducted before the start of the 1st semester of the following academic year.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VI PAMANTASAN NG CABUYAO STUDENT ELECTIONS > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: h. Election Complaints, Petitions, and Sanctions i. All complaints, petitions, and sanctions shall be imposed, after due process, to any candidate/party that has committed any offenses. ii. Complaints of a party/candidate against another party/ candidate arising from any violation of specific provisions in these guidelines shall be lodged before the SCOMELEC for preliminary investigation. iii. Complaints, petitions, and sanctions shall be acted upon with due process. Decisions shall be final and executory upon the concurrence of the SCOMELEC. iv. Any defeated candidate or interested party may file an election protest with the SCOMELEC within one week after the receipt of the decision. v. Violation of any provision of the guidelines shall render any candidate/party liable to appropriate penalty from SCOMELEC without prejudice to the sanctions to be given by the school authorities. i. Failure of Election i. In case of Failure of Election, an Alliance of Recognized Student Organization shall be formed by the SASD thru snap election. Only the Presidents of the current student organizations can vote. ii. The following may be considered as reasons for an election failure: • No candidate signified interest to run in any or majority of number of positions both for USG, CSG and student councils • Candidate/s did not receive 50% plus one votes. • Massive election-related cheating. iii. A snap election for Alliance of Recognized Student Organization shall be composed of all Presidents of the student organizations.

text: CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-13 Section 1. General Policies 1. The Guidance and Counseling Department provides a comprehensive developmental guidance and counseling program which intends to develop well-functioning individuals and to ensure utilization of their fullest potentials. 2. Suhay refers to support, which reflects the encompassing role of the Guidance and Counseling department in ensuring the academic, social, emotional and personal development of the students. 3. PNC shall ensure confidentiality of all guidance and counseling student records. Consent shall be secured by the Guidance and Counseling Department to all concerned counselee. However, records may be released to concerned department under certain circumstances: a. If the student/personnel present/presents a serious danger to self or other person(s); b. If there is a suspicion or actual incident of abuse or neglect; c. Presence of a valid subpoena is issued for concerned student/ personnel records, or d. Student/personnel records are otherwise subject to a court order or other legal process requiring disclosure. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. The following are the guidance services provided to all students and personnel of Pamantasan ng Cabuyao

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: a. Individual Inventory Service. i. This maintains a record of students' study habits, health and well-being, personality assessment, career questionnaire, counseling sessions, scholastic progress, and other data relevant to their development and progress in TVL, senior, college, and graduate school. Basic inquiries about family and education shall be maintained at the Office of the University Registrar through a centralized student information system. ii. Student Cumulative Record (PNC:SDAS-FO-36) is filled out by the students online or via google forms before the semester ends. This applies to all new or first year students. For continuing education students, PNC:SDAS-FO-37 shall be accomplished by the students online or via google forms. b. Counseling Service. i. The counseling services provide assistance to students in making decision about their problems. The following counseling sessions are made available for all students with academic, personal, interpersonal, career concerns and other problems affecting them. These may be done online or remote. • Individual Counseling/e-Counseling. A one-on-one session between counselor and counselee. • Group Counseling. This service is intended for students to share a common need or concern that is usually developmental in nature • Exit Interview. Exiting students (graduating and transferees) shall undergo exit interview before signing their clearance. Exit Interview Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-38) shall be distributed to student leavers. ii. Counseling Session Report Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-39) shall be accomplished to document the results of the counseling session. iii. An Informed Consent Form (PNC:SDAS-FO-40) shall be

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: accomplished and duly signed by the counselee, parent/ guardian (for below 18 years old counselee) and the counselor prior to start of any counseling sessions. This allows counselee to become partners in assessing best possible management that accord with their own needs and values. iv. Following are the responsibilities of the counselee • Take an active role in the counseling process and working toward the goals set by the counselor. If it is determined that the counselee is not working towards identified goals, the counseling relationship may be terminated. • Come to scheduled appointments on time. Tardiness of 15 minutes or more for a scheduled appointment will mean rescheduling of the counseling session. • Call and cancel appointment if counselee will not be able to come. For two or more "no shows," it will be assumed that the counselee is no longer interested in counseling and will be removed from the schedule. • Excessive tardiness (three or more late arrivals) will mean forfeiture of counseling services. Two or more cancellations will mean that I/my child will be removed from the schedule. c. Referral Service. It is a support system that may address students with special needs. Members of the PNC (UC) community may refer student/s with perceived academic, social, personal behavioral problem. This shall be documented thru PNC-SDAS-FO-13. d. Follow-up Service. This is to determine the success or failure of the counseling session/s conducted online or in-person. Further, students who were referred due to academic failure shall be called for academic follow-up by the counselor. e. Career Development Service. In coordination with the Placement, Alumni, and Linkages Department, these

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: activities intend to attain competencies needed to prepare for meaningful, satisfying, and productive career of PnC (UC) students. f. Enhancement Program i. Orientation and learning sessions shall be facilitated by the Guidance and Counseling Department online or in-person. ii. Topics may include but not limited to the following: • Anxiety Management; • Basic Dynamics of Communication; • Career Development Activities; • Coping Strategies; • Effective Study Skills; • Enhancing Leadership Skills; • Enhancing Self-Concept; • Getting in Touch with True Self; • Job Interview Training Program; • Managing Emotions in Times of Uncertainty; • Overcoming Shyness and Pessimism; • Psychological Distress; • Psychological First Aid in Managing Thoughts; • Resume Writing; • Stress Coping Mechanisms; • Surviving SHS or college life; • Time Management; • Understanding Human Sexuality; • Well-Being or Self-Care; and • Personality Development g. Consultation Service. It brings together the needed assistance for positive impact on student achievement and formation. i. Teacher Consultation. The collaborative effort of teacher and counselor to discuss student need and growth ensures a productive teamwork. ii. Parent Consultation. The partnership of home and school is vital for student development. Parents/Guardians may be called for an online or in-person meetings. Invitation could

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VII GUIDANCE AND COUNSELING PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: be documented through (PNC-SDAS-FO-43). h. Testing Service. Psychological tests are administered to assess student abilities, interests, skills, and achievement. Outcomes are beneficial for addressing individual/group needs. Individual tests will be administered to address the unique needs of students as they arise. i. Grade 11 –Occupational Aptitude Survey and Interest Schedule (OASIS-3). This test helps students identify their career aptitudes and interests and find careers that align with their strengths ii. Grade 12 – Career Orientation Placement and Evaluation Survey (COPES). This test intends to measure personal values in the workplace. This will help students to find occupational areas that match their personal values. iii. First Year College – Scholastic Ability Test for Adults (SATA). This test is designed to measure scholastic competence of the student to highlight individual strengths, weaknesses and areas of competence iv. Second Year College – Occupational Aptitude Survey and Interest Schedule (OASIS-3). This test helps students identify their career aptitudes and interests and find careers that align with their strengths. v. Third Year – Manchester Personality Test. This test is designed to identify and report on key personality traits likely to have a high impact on behavior and success at work and to highlight individual strengths, weaknesses and areas of competence. vi. Fourth Year – Career Attitudes and Strategies Inventory (CASI) and BarOn Emotional Quotient Test for internship students, CASI will assess students' likelihood of job stability or change, potential career obstacles, or areas for further development. Meanwhile, BarOn measures the emotional and social behavior of students. vii. Graduate School Students – BarOn Emotional Quotient Test and MD5 Mental Ability Test. The latter is designed to assess the students' ability to use logic and reasoning to solve cryptic problems, under a tight time pressure.

text: i. Research. The Guidance and Counseling Department shall analyze and interpret empirical data, which intends to continuously improve its services. Results of psychological tests shall be analyzed and interpreted and submitted to academic heads for continuous improvement.

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER VIII ALUMNI PROGRAM AND SERVICES > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: CHAPTER VIII ALUMNI PROGRAM AND SERVICES PNC:SDAS-GU-14 Section 1. General Policies 1. The Placement, Alumni, and Linkage Department shall facilitate the alumni programs and services. 2. The PALD Director shall collaborate with the Alumni Regent in carrying out the activities outlined in this guideline. 3. PALD shall mobilize Placement, Alumni, and Linkage Coordinator for each academic department. They shall assist PALD Director in all aspects of alumni relations delivery. Appointment paper shall be issued by the Vice President for Student Development and Auxiliary Services upon endorsement by the PALD Director. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Alumni Tracking. a. In order to track alumni, the Alumni Profile Tracer Form must be completed (PNC:SDAS-FO-41). The form mentioned above can be filled out in a variety of ways, including in person at the university, via email, social media, and other online platforms. b. The report on alumni tracking will be forwarded to the Research and Development Department for analysis and interpretation. 2. Alumni Placement a. The Office shall manage career development service, including placement activities and Career Fair for graduating students. These include job posting, in-campus/remote recruitment, among others. PALD may collaborate with shop owners or institutions to establish Alumni Card rewards and privileges. 5. Monitoring of Alumni Activities a. The University's alumni welcome-back event is called "PAG-UWI". It can be an annual grand reunion of alumni or reunion held every five years. This will be held during the PNC (UC) Foundation Celebration.

Organizing PAGSALUDO! A Tribute for New Passers. In determining the awardees for PAGSALUDO!, the following shall be observed: a. Board examination passers. text: CHAPTER IX LIBRARY SERVICES PNC:AA-GU-16 Section 1. General Policies 1. Library Service Hours. The library is open from Mondays to Fridays from 8am-5pm. The library is open to all bonafide students, teaching and non-teaching personnel of the University. b. Alumni and outside researchers may avail themselves of the resources subject to the rules and regulations of the library. c. eLibrary can be accessed by the students, teaching and non-teaching personnel, and outside researchers anytime, anywhere. d. The University Library shall enforce all national and local government laws relative to any related health-posing-risk situations. e. University students, teaching, and non-teaching personnel. i. Personal belongings shall be deposited at the depository shelf at the entrance of the library. ii. Library clients must bring with them their valuables such as money, jewelry, and cellular phones. The library will not be held liable for lost valuables. iii. Clients may use any material, shelved, or stores in the stack areas, and any equipment or facilities that are designated for use except where restrictions are established by the

section_path: PART 3. STUDENT SUCCESS > CHAPTER IX LIBRARY SERVICES > Section 1. General Policies

text: 3. Library Users Conduct and Study Atmosphere a. The following shall be permitted at the University Library: i. section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES
text: Welcome to the Code of Conduct and Disciplinary Procedures section of the Student Manual. At Pamantasan ng Cabuyao, we believe in fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful learning environment for all members of our community. This section outlines the expectations, rights, and responsibilities that guide our interactions and behaviors as students. The Code of Conduct serves as a framework that upholds our institution's values, promotes ethical conduct, and ensures the well-being of everyone on campus. It sets forth the standards of behavior that we expect from each student, emphasizing integrity, honesty, respect, and accountability. In addition to the Code of Conduct, this section provides you with an overview of the disciplinary procedures in place to address violations of the Code. These procedures are designed to be fair, transparent, and aimed at promoting learning, growth, and corrective action when necessary. It is important to familiarize yourself with these procedures to understand your rights and the consequences associated with any misconduct. We believe in the power of education to transform lives, and our commitment to a positive and respectful community is at the heart of that belief. As a student at PnC, you have the responsibility to uphold the values outlined in the Code of Conduct and contribute to an inclusive and safe environment for yourself and your fellow students. Remember, the Code of Conduct is not just a set of rules; it is a commitment to shared values and principles that shape our collective experience as students. Let us embrace these guidelines as we embark on our journey of learning, growth, and community at PnC.

text: CHAPTER II STUDENT DISCIPLINE PNC:SDAS-GU-05 Section 1. General Policies 1. Disciplinary actions are corrective measures imposed on students who failed to comply with the provisions on the expected student decorum. The primary objective of these actions is to guide the erring students to follow the path of right conduct. Severe disciplinary actions, however, may be imposed on certain cases as the circumstances may warrant. 2. The imposition of the appropriate disciplinary action shall be progressive in character, taking into account the previous violations committed by the offender. If the offender was already warned because of a minor offense that he/she committed, a second violation involving the same minor offense or a more serious offense shall be meted suspension/ non-readmission/exclusion/ expulsion depending on the gravity of the offense. a. A Reprimand shall serve as a warning (PNC:SDAS-FO-10) that any future violation of this guideline shall be a ground for the imposition of a more severe penalty. b. A Warning is a written notice (PNC:SDAS-FO-10) to the offender that continuation or repetition of the wrongful conduct within a period of time stated in the warning may be a cause for more severe disciplinary action. c. A Suspension is a penalty in which a student is denied or deprived of attendance in classes which shall be imposed for serious or major offenses or willful violations of this guideline. Serious or major offenses may warrant the imposition of a longer duration of suspension for the student concerned, which could range from a whole term to an entire academic year, as the assigned Panel for the case would deem appropriate and just.

text: CHAPTER III STUDENT GRIEVANCE PNC:SDAS-GU-06 Section 1. General Policies 1. Grievance against any member of the PnC-UC community should be initially settled with the person concerned through sincere dialogue and discussion. 2. If, for whatever reason, a student/s does/do not wish to communicate directly with the concerned person to discuss his/her complaint or grievance, he/she should file a written complaint with the Program Chair or Dean/Principal who has supervision over the teaching personnel for academic-related concerns. Non-academic-related concerns shall be filed at the Student Affairs and Services Department. 3. It is only when the initial discussion fails that one may resort to formal procedure for settling offense / complaints. 4. A case conference shall be conducted to resolve grievances. First option is to settle the case amicably between parties involved. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. All complaints shall be addressed by the concerned office. For example: a. Issues about academic probations shall be handled by the Office of the Dean/Principal. b. Issues about the performance or behavior of the support staff shall be lodged with the Human Resource Management Department of the University. c. Issues about possible crimes etc. shall be filed with the Student Affairs and Services Department d. Regarding issues about health, the student shall contact the University Health Department

Issues about grades, examinations, excused absences, class policies, etc. shall be resolved under the following considerations: • Teaching personnel have primary responsibility in all these areas and are charged with carrying out those responsibilities in a professional manner and in accordance with the policies issued by the University. • The Dean/Principal, in coordination with the Program Chair, has the authority and responsibility to deal with changes of grades in special cases such as those which might involve the teaching personnel who have left the university or unprofessional teaching personnel conduct in assigning the grade. • Student/s should be aware that neither the Program Chair nor the Dean/Principal can require a teaching personnel to change a properly assigned course grade. • Issues of disagreement about answers to test questions are decided solely by the teaching personnel. • If the student/s is/are unable to resolve the problem with the teaching personnel, he/she may file a written complaint with the Program Chair or the Dean/Principal. The Dean/Principal is the mediator of any academic grievance ii. Issues about teaching personnel performance or teaching personnel behavior should be lodged with the Program Chair or Dean/Principal. • The student/s shall file his/her written complaint with the Program Chair who has supervision over the teaching personnel. • The Program Chair shall exert effort to resolve the problem.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER III STUDENT GRIEVANCE > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: • If the effort fails, the Program Chair shall refer the written complaint to the Dean/Principal. • Depending on the gravity of the teaching personnel performance or behavior, the Dean/Principal shall refer the matter to the Vice President for Academic Affairs and Human Resource Management Department. • If the teaching personnel behavior in question involves allegation of sexual harassment, the Program Chair and the Dean/Principal shall immediately refer the complaint to the SASD. iii. Procedures • The student/s can request for an appointment with the Program Chair and/or file a written complaint or grievance. • The concerned administrator shall study the merit of the complaint and must do the necessary action within three (3) to five (5) working days upon receipt of the complaint. • If the student alleges sexual harassment, the Program Chair shall immediately inform the Dean/Principal and the latter shall forward the information or written complaint to the SASD • Alternatively, or in addition, a student/s shall have the option of getting counsel and advice from the Guidance Counselor. • If the student fails to get the necessary action, his/ her complaint shall be referred to the Vice President for Academic Affairs. S/he is expected to act on it by investigating the matter from both parties. c. A class complaint against a Teaching or Non-Teaching Personnel i. If the class complains against a teaching or non-teaching personnel, the class shall try first to present the complaint to the teaching or non-teaching personnel concerned. ii. The said written complaint shall be signed by 50% plus one of the students. Dean/Principal/Department Head shall

text: be furnished a copy. If the complaint is settled, a written report shall be submitted by the concerned teaching or non-teaching personnel to the Dean/Principal concerned iii. If the initial step fails to receive the necessary action, the written complaint shall be forwarded to the Dean/Principal/ Department Head. The class shall elect a committee of three representatives to see the Dean/Principal/ Department Head. The Dean/Principal/Department Head has three working days to investigate and settle the complaint. iv. If the class members feel that necessary actions on their complaint have not been taken within the prescribed period or if the Dean/Principal/Department Head fails to settle the complaint, the case shall be referred to the Division Head concerned. d. Guidance and Counseling Department shall maintain a copy of all decisions of student grievance cases that shall serve as reference on the issuance of Certificate of Good Moral Character Certificate and Certificate of Deportment. e. The complaints of non-students, namely, Pamantasan ng Cabuyao teaching and non-teaching personnel against PNC students shall also be entertained by the SASD and shall also be covered by its standard operating procedures.
