text: CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING PNC:SDAS-GU-07 Section 1. General Policies 1. Through the Student Affairs and Services Department, the University must create a Drug-Free Committee (DFC). The DFC is responsible for developing and putting into action drug testing policies, which include programs for drug prevention, control, and education. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Notification a. Before full implementation, Pamantasan ng Cabuyao shall inform the school community of the prescribed guidelines and ensure that they are included in the Student Manual with proper notice to all students and parents on the procedure and manner in which the random drug testing shall be conducted. The administration of the drug test shall not be prevented by the failure to return the acknowledgment receipt. b. Through the University Student Government, students will be consulted about the mandated drug testing procedure. The consultation process must be completed by the end of February of the academic year prior to the one in which the planned mandatory testing will take place. 2. Samples a. The random sampling includes every student enrolled at the institution. b. The quantity of samples need to result in a 95% statistical confidence level for the entire student body.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: c. To determine the number of students who will be subject to random drug testing, the Drug-Free Committee (DFC) will employ Slovin's formula. 3. Selection of Samples a. The School Nurse shall serve as the Drug Testing Coordinator. S/he shall convene the Drug-Free Committee within five (5) days from the receipt of notice. The Drug-Free Committee shall be composed of the following: i. Director, Student Affairs and Services Department (Chair); ii. Full-time Teaching Personnel Representative; iii. Parent Representative; iv. Student Representative; v. University Health Department Representative; and vi. Student Discipline Officer (Secretary). b. The Drug-Free Committee will administer a random selection of those to be tested on the testing day. c. The drug-free committee will make sure the random selection method is fair and impartial. d. The selection procedure will be done at random using a lottery that may be computerized or in any other way that the committee may decide. e. Students will be chosen at random and tested for drugs on the same day. The list of the chosen students and their class schedule will be sent to the student discipline officer, who will then go to their classrooms to collect them or send an online invitation before heading straight to the University Health Department. f. The chosen students will be questioned about any prescription medications, vitamins, or food supplements they have taken during the last five (5) days before the test. The Drug Testing Coordinator must preserve the list and refer to it when assessing the results of the confirmatory drug test.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: g. When collecting urine samples, the laboratory must adhere to the DOH's recommended procedures. To prevent contaminating the samples and tampering with them, general measures must always be followed. The DOH-required rules must be posted in prominent locations around the campus. h. The monitor assigned to ensure the integrity of the collection process should be of the same gender as the student. i. The drug testing shall be done in the University in coordination with City Hospital or accredited partner for a drug-testing laboratory free of charge. j. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the random drug testing. 4. Treatment of Random Drug Testing Results a. The results of the test shall be strictly confidential. The University shall not publish or post results whether positive or negative. b. Any person who violates the rules of confidentiality of the results and selection shall be liable under Section 72 of RA 9165 and such other appropriate laws. c. In case the results are positive at the screening level, the same specimen shall immediately be submitted for confirmation observing all strict chain of custody procedures and confidentiality of records. d. If a student is "confirmed" to be using a dangerous drug, the following shall be observed. i. The University Health Department receives an official report from the laboratory in a sealed envelope. ii. The SASD shall inform the parent and the student of the results and how the information is regarded with utmost secrecy and confidentiality.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: • The SASD shall remind the student that divulging the results with anybody will be at his/her own risk; and • That if possible, the information should remain in the confines of their house. iii. The SASD, parent, and the student shall then prepare for a case conference to discuss issues of drug use and possible dependency. iv. The Drug Testing Coordinator shall refer the student and his/her parent to a government-owned facility or DOH-accredited government physician to determine the student's dependency level. v. A date and venue shall be selected for the case conference. • Date should be agreeable to all concerned in the case conference (Parent, Student, Drug Testing Coordinator and DOH Accredited Physician) • Venue should have a semblance of privacy (preferably in a room, with an office table where group discussions and individual sessions can be done.) vi. Following shall be discussed during the case conference. • Drug dependency level of the student shall be evaluated; • Cross reference of information shall be validated from the parent and Drug Testing Coordinator. • Treatment planning for the student shall be discussed and presented to the student and parent; • If a student (below 18 years of age) is found to be a drug dependent, SASD shall refer him/her to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) or local social worker for counseling and other intervention. • The Parent and the student may choose to enroll the student in a private rehabilitation center or program or opt to avail the rehabilitation services of the government through a DOH-accredited facility. • If a child opts for government service, the DOH treatment and rehabilitation centers nearest to the area can provide services. • If the parent and student would opt for private

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER IV CONDUCT OF DRUG TESTING > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: services, appropriate referrals will be done, taking note of the progress of treatment on a regular basis. • Trained guidance counselors can also be utilized. • The Drug Testing Coordinator shall individually inform each student and parent concerned regarding the results. • Positive confirmatory drug test results, as specified in DepEd and CHED Orders, shall not be a ground for expulsion or any disciplinary action against the student and should not be reflected in any and all academic records. Under no circumstances shall the results be used to incriminate any student for further legal action which may result to administrative/civil/criminal liabilities. • Likewise, consistent with the requirement of confidentiality, the results of drug tests conducted pursuant to CHED or DepEd Orders, shall not be used as evidence in any court of tribunal, where the subject student stands to be accused of any crime or felony, and for any other purpose. • The student shall then undergo the prescribed intervention program under the supervision of the DOH-accredited facility or physician, or private practitioners, or social worker, in consultation with the parent. Such process of observation and counseling shall be done in coordination with SASD and Guidance Counselor. • If student shows no signs of improvement, recovery, or fails the drug test the second time, the DOH-accredited facility or physician, may make a recommendation to the student, parent and SASD to have the student referred to a DOH-accredited facility suited to the student's level of dependency. If another drug testing is conducted for another period on the same student population, and the student is found positive the second time, the school shall proceed in accordance with Section 61, R.A. 9165. • If the parents refuse to act, the University shall proceed in accordance to Sec. 61 of RA 9165 without prejudice to the provision of Section 73, RA 9165.

text: 5. Training of Guidance Counselors. The University will implement the guidance counselor training program to improve their abilities in managing drug abuse prevention initiatives and dealing with drug dependency cases. Counselors at schools and other appropriately competent medical personnel should be encouraged to get DOH accreditation.

text: CHAPTER V SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINE PNC:AF-GU-28 Section 1. General Policies 1. The purpose of social media use is to effectively engage and communicate with stakeholders, including students, personnel, alumni, and the general public. 2. Social media can enhance the University's reputation and visibility, share news and updates, promote events and activities, facilitate dialogue and conversation, and provide valuable resources and information to the community. 3. It can also be used for recruitment, retention, fundraising efforts, as well as for research and academic purposes. 4. All personnel and students of the University are expected to use social media responsibly, ethically, and professionally, consistent with the University' philosophy and objectives. a. Professionalism: All personnel and students of the University should maintain a professional tone and demeanor when using social media. This includes refraining from profanity, discriminatory language, personal attacks, or other unprofessional behavior. b. Confidentiality: All personnel and students of the University must maintain confidentiality and protect the privacy of the organization, its clients, and stakeholders. This means refraining from sharing confidential information, trade secrets, or other sensitive information through social media channels. c. Respect for others: All personnel and students of the University should treat others with respect, civility, and courtesy. This includes refraining from engaging in bullying, harassment, or other forms of inappropriate behavior.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER V SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINE > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: d. Accuracy: All content posted on social media channels must be accurate, truthful, and reliable. Misrepresenting the University can harm the organization's reputation and credibility. e. Compliance: All personnel and students of the University must comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and policies governing social media use. This includes complying with copyright laws, trademark laws, and other intellectual property laws. f. Transparency: All personnel and students of the University should be transparent when using social media channels. This includes disclosing any affiliations, relationships, or financial interests that may create a conflict of interest. Section 2. Specific Policies 1. Category of Offenses. Offenses defined under this rule shall be considered as serious offense. 2. Approving Unethical, Offensive and Libelous Messages Using any Electronic Means. Any personnel or student of the university who, being an administrator of any page, group, group chat, and other online groups available through electronic means, will approve any post or messages which is unethical, offensive or libelous shall, after due process shall be: i. 1st Offense. Suspended for a period of not less than 1 week but not more than 6 weeks. The number of weeks may be shortened through community service at the discretion of disciplining authority. ii. 2nd Offense. Suspensed for 1 semester. iii. 3rd Offense. Permanent Dismissal. 3. Posting Unethical, Offensive and Libelous Messages Using Any Electronic Means. Any personnel or student of the university who will post any messages which is unethical, offensive or libelous shall, after due process shall be:

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER V SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINE > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: i. 1st Offense. Suspended for a period of not less than 1 week but not more than 6 weeks. The number of weeks may be shortened through community service at the discretion of disciplining authority ii. 2nd Offense. Suspended for 1 semester. iii. 3rd Offense. Permanent Dismissal. 4. Sharing Unethical, Offensive, and Libelous Messages Using Any Electronic Means. Any personnel or student of the university who will share any post which is unethical, offensive or libelous shall, after due process shall be: i. 1st Offense. Suspended for a period of not less than 1 week but not more than 3 weeks. The number of weeks may be shortened through community service at the discretion of disciplining authority. ii. 2nd Offense. Suspended for 1 semester. iii. 3rd Offense. Permanent Dismissal. 5. Reacting to Unethical, Offensive and Libelous Messages Using Any Electronic Means. Any personnel or student of the university who react in any manner to a post or comment which is unethical, offensive or libelous shall, after due process shall be: i. 1st Offense. Suspended for a period of not less than 2 days but not more than 5 days. The number of days may be shortened through community service at the discretion of disciplining authority. ii. 2nd Offense. Suspended for a period of not less than 1 week but not more than 3 weeks. The number of weeks may be shortened through community service at the discretion of disciplining authority. iii. 3rd Offense. Suspended for 1 semester iv. 4th Offense. Permanent Dismissal.

section_path: PART 4. CODE OF CONDUCT AND DISCIPLINARY PROCEDURES > CHAPTER V SOCIAL MEDIA GUIDELINE > Section 2. Specific Policies
text: 6. Nature of the Offense. Offenses defined under this rule is considered as a continuing offense and hence, refusal by the student to delete or remove any unethical, offensive or libelous messages or post constitutes a continuing violation and may be considered another count(s) of violation. 7. Guidelines in handling student and teaching and non-teaching personnel discipline shall be in accordance with PNC:SDAS-FU-05 Student Discipline and PNC:AF-GU-22 Personnel Discipline.
